description: A large and brightly colored pheasant species native to the Indian subcontinent, famous for the male's iridescent blue-green plumage and spectacular fan-like courtship train.
habitat: Deciduous forests, scrub jungles, agricultural fields, and semi-arid countryside.
diet: Omnivorous; feeds on seeds, insects, fruits, small reptiles, and amphibians.
distribution: Widespread resident across India, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
interesting_facts: The Indian Peafowl is the National Bird of India.
The male's ornamental train is formed by elongated upper-tail covert feathers, not the actual tail.
Their loud, piercing call 'may-awe' is often used as a monsoon call and predator alarm.

description: A member of the cuckoo order known for its resonant, rising 'koo-oo' call heard extensively during spring and summer. Males are glossy black with ruby eyes; females are speckled brown.
habitat: Woodlands, gardens, urban trees, and plantations.
diet: Frugivorous as adults; also consumes caterpillars, insects, and small fruit.
distribution: Common resident throughout South Asia, Southeast Asia, and southern China.
interesting_facts: They are brood parasites that predominantly lay their eggs in House Crow and Jungle Crow nests.
Unlike many parasitic cuckoos, the chicks do not aggressively eject host eggs from the nest.

description: A medium-sized corvid of slender build with a charcoal-black body, glossy black cap and face, and a distinct silvery-grey nape and breast collar.
habitat: Towns, cities, villages, coastal regions, and agricultural settlements.
diet: Highly omnivorous scavenger; eats food scraps, grains, small invertebrates, carrion, and eggs.
distribution: Native to the Indian subcontinent; widely introduced along Indian Ocean ports.
interesting_facts: Virtually never found away from human settlements.
Known for extraordinary cognitive problem-solving, facial recognition, and communal roosting.

description: A stocky brown starling with a black hood, bright yellow bill, yellow legs, and bare yellow skin around the eyes.
habitat: Open country, farmlands, roadside avenues, urban settlements, and gardens.
diet: Omnivorous; insects, fruits, grains, flower nectar, and household leftovers.
distribution: Native to tropical and subtropical South and Central Asia.
interesting_facts: Mating pairs form strong lifelong monogamous bonds.
Possesses a vast vocal repertoire of whistles, clicks, chirps, and vocal mimicry.

description: A vibrant lime-green parakeet with a long graduated tail and red bill. Adult males display a fine pink neck ring paired with a black chin stripe.
habitat: Woodlands, parks, agricultural fields, orchards, and urban gardens.
diet: Granivorous and frugivorous; seeds, nuts, berries, cultivated grains, and blossoms.
distribution: Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, with feral urban colonies worldwide.
interesting_facts: Roosts communally in massive flocks numbering thousands in dense city trees.
Popularly known in Indian literature and classical folklore as the 'Tota'.

description: A brownish-black songbird with an upright crest, scalloped breast plumage, and a bright crimson-red patch under the base of the tail.
habitat: Scrub jungles, orchards, cultivated fields, urban parks, and domestic gardens.
diet: Fruits, berries, flower nectar, insects, and tender leaf shoots.
distribution: Native across the entire Indian subcontinent and Sri Lanka.
interesting_facts: Highly territorial and vocal, producing cheerful, bubbly whistling songs.
Plays a vital ecological role in seed dispersal and pollination of forest plants.

description: Easily identified by its tall pointed crest, red patch behind each eye, white cheeks, red vent, and loud three-note musical call.
habitat: Hill forest clearings, scrublands, plantations, gardens, and wooded valleys.
diet: Berries, small fruits, insects, and flower nectar.
distribution: Native to tropical Asia, common across southern and eastern India.
interesting_facts: Its song resembles a brisk and lively 'kink-a-joo' whistling phrase.
Often nests close to human dwellings, in ornamental garden hedges.

description: A dimorphic chat: males are glossy black with a white shoulder stripe and chestnut-red vent; females are smoky brown with a paler chestnut vent.
habitat: Stony scrublands, open dry deciduous woodlands, railway tracks, and rural edges.
diet: Invertebrates, beetles, termites, ants, and spiders.
distribution: Endemic to South Asia (India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka).
interesting_facts: Characteristically cocks its tail straight up over its back while foraging on the ground.
Often perches atop rocks, fence posts, and low bushes to deliver short chirping songs.

description: A striking black-and-white songbird with a pied pattern, white belly, white wingbars, and a long tail held erect.
habitat: Gardens, open deciduous forests, urban parks, mangrove margins, and orchards.
diet: Insects, earthworms, caterpillars, grasshoppers, and occasionally flower nectar.
distribution: Native to South and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: Celebrated as one of Asia's finest dawn-chorus singers, delivering rich melodic tunes.
It is the National Bird of Bangladesh.

description: A large non-parasitic cuckoo with a glossy purple-black body, bright chestnut-rufous wings, ruby-red eyes, and a long heavy tail.
habitat: Dense scrub, hedges, tall grassland marshes, forest edges, and rural backyards.
diet: Insects, snails, lizards, frogs, small snakes, and bird eggs.
distribution: Widespread across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: Also known as the Crow Pheasant; builds its own deep domed cup nest of twigs.
Produces a deep booming resonant call 'coop-coop-coop' that carries across fields.

description: An all-black passerine with a distinctive forked tail, sleek plumage, and a fierce, bold territorial temperament.
habitat: Open agricultural fields, roadside telephone lines, pastures, and light woods.
diet: Mainly flying insects like dragonflies, moths, beetles, and termites caught on the wing.
distribution: Widespread resident across South and East Asia.
interesting_facts: Nicknamed the 'King Crow' for its fearless habit of mobbing larger birds like hawks and eagles.
Often rides on the backs of grazing cattle to snap up disturbed grasshoppers.

description: A large tree kingfisher with a bright turquoise-blue back and wings, chocolate-brown head and flanks, bright white throat and breast, and heavy red bill.
habitat: Farmlands, open woodlands, irrigation canals, village ponds, and roadside wires.
diet: Lizards, crustaceans, small rodents, large insects, frogs, and fish.
distribution: From the eastern Mediterranean through South Asia and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: Does not rely exclusively on water; frequently hunts far from rivers in agricultural fields.
Emits a loud, ringing chattering laugh from exposed tree perches.

description: A sparrow-sized kingfisher with radiant metallic cyan-blue upperparts, vibrant orange underparts, a short tail, and long dagger-like bill.
habitat: Clear, slow-flowing rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, and mangrove creeks.
diet: Specializes in small freshwater fish, water beetles, and aquatic dragonfly nymphs.
distribution: Eurasia and North Africa, resident across the Indian subcontinent.
interesting_facts: Dives with eyelids covered by a transparent nictitating membrane to spot prey underwater.
Can consume up to its own body weight in fish each day.

description: A slender dove with a warm rosy-brown breast, greyish head, and a conspicuous white-spotted black chessboard patch on the nape.
habitat: Open dry woodlands, gardens, cultivated fields, urban fringes, and scrub.
diet: Grains, grass seeds, fallen seeds, and small cultivated crops.
distribution: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia; introduced elsewhere.
interesting_facts: Produces a gentle, rhythmic cooing call: 'kroo-kruk-kroo... kroo-kroo'.
Performs a dramatic courtship display flight with steep climbing and clapping wings.

description: A stout dove with blue-grey plumage, twin black wing bars, iridescent purple and emerald neck feathers, and reddish feet.
habitat: Cliffs, historic monuments, railway stations, bridges, and city buildings.
diet: Seeds, cereal grains, human food waste, and green vegetation.
distribution: Worldwide cosmopolitan distribution; abundant across South Asia.
interesting_facts: Possesses magnetoreception allowing extraordinary homing navigation abilities over hundreds of miles.
Both parents feed their squabs with nutrient-dense crop milk.

description: A small, sturdy songbird: males have patterned grey and brown backs, grey crown, and a black bib; females are sandy buff-brown overall.
habitat: Human settlements, agricultural homesteads, town centers, and grain markets.
diet: Grains, weed seeds, cultivated crops, insects, and breadcrumbs.
distribution: Native to Eurasia and North Africa, introduced globally.
interesting_facts: Strongly associated with rural tiled roofs and traditional grain storage in India.
World Sparrow Day is celebrated annually on March 20 to raise conservation awareness.

description: A small stocky heron appearing dull streaky brown and camouflaged when standing, but transforming into gleaming white when taking flight due to snowy wings.
habitat: Paddy fields, marshes, village ponds, roadside ditches, and riverbanks.
diet: Frogs, small fish, aquatic insects, dragonflies, and crustaceans.
distribution: Indian subcontinent, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and western Iran.
interesting_facts: Popularly known in Hindi as 'Andha Bagula' (Blind Heron) because it stands motionless until stepped upon.
During breeding season, adults develop rich maroon mantle feathers and long white head plumes.

description: A compact white heron with a short thick yellow bill and dark legs, acquiring rich orange-buff plumes on the crown, chest, and back during breeding season.
habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural fields, wetlands, and pastures alongside grazing herds.
diet: Grasshoppers, crickets, flies, beetles, ticks, and small amphibians.
distribution: Cosmopolitan across warm temperate and tropical zones.
interesting_facts: Maintains a mutualistic relationship with livestock, feeding on insects stirred up by their footsteps.
Has expanded its global range faster than almost any other wading bird.

description: A graceful pure white wading bird with an all-black bill, long black legs, and contrasting bright yellow feet ('golden slippers').
habitat: Lakes, estuaries, coastal mudflats, rice fields, and shallow riverbeds.
diet: Small fish, frogs, worms, crustaceans, and aquatic larvae.
distribution: Widespread across southern Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australasia.
interesting_facts: Shuffles its bright yellow feet in shallow silt to flush out hidden fish.
Once heavily hunted for its delicate breeding plumes used in Victorian women's hats.

description: A diminutive nectar feeder with a down-curved bill. Breeding males are glossy metallic dark purple-black; females and eclipse males are olive-brown with yellow undersides.
habitat: Gardens, scrub forests, flowering deciduous woodlands, and agricultural orchards.
diet: Flower nectar, spiders, small insects, and fruit juice.
distribution: South Asia, parts of Southeast Asia, and the Arabian Peninsula.
interesting_facts: Can hover briefly in front of floral blossoms like a miniature hummingbird while sipping nectar.
Builds an intricate hanging pouch nest made of cobwebs, lichen, and bark.

description: An active, tiny warbler with bright olive-green upperparts, creamy-white underparts, a rufous-chestnut cap, and an upright cocked tail.
habitat: Urban gardens, hedgerows, scrub jungles, plantations, and deciduous thickets.
diet: Tiny insects, caterpillars, beetles, bugs, and flower nectar.
distribution: Throughout the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: Famous as 'Darzee' in Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book.
Stitches large living tree leaves together using plant fibers and cobwebs to form a cradled nest pocket.

description: A dazzling songbird: males are striking golden-yellow with contrasting jet-black wings and tail; females and juveniles are dull greenish-yellow.
habitat: Canopy of deciduous forests, riverine river woods, plantations, and large urban gardens.
diet: Insects, caterpillars, berries, figs, and cherries.
distribution: Breeds in Eurasia, winters or passes through parts of South Asia and Africa.
interesting_facts: Possesses a clear, flute-like whistling song described as 'weela-wee-ooo'.
Despite its bright yellow colors, it blends remarkably well into the sunlit forest canopy.

description: A medium-sized hornbill with brownish-grey plumage, pale underparts, and an arched blackish bill topped with a pointed casque.
habitat: Deciduous woodlands, large roadside banyan and peepal trees, and urban parks.
diet: Mainly wild figs, berries, and fruits, plus insects and small lizards.
distribution: Endemic to the Indian subcontinent.
interesting_facts: The female seals herself inside a tree hollow with mud during incubation, leaving only a feeding slit.
Essential keystone seed dispersers for major fig species (Ficus religiosa and Ficus benghalensis).

description: A medium raptor with rich chestnut-rufous body and wings contrasting with a gleaming white head, neck, and breast, and yellow talons.
habitat: Coastal wetlands, tidal estuaries, fishing harbors, rivers, and mangrove creeks.
diet: Dead fish, small crabs, water snakes, frogs, and scraps stolen from other birds.
distribution: Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, and Australasia.
interesting_facts: Considered the contemporary representation of the mythical bird 'Garuda' in Hindu traditions.
A skilled aerial kleptoparasite that harasses other birds mid-air to drop their prey.

description: A buoyant, opportunistic raptor with dark brown plumage, angled wings, and a distinct shallow-forked rudder-like tail.
habitat: Cities, municipal dumps, abattoirs, open countryside, riverbanks, and coastlines.
diet: Carrion, household refuse, discarded fish, rodents, and small birds.
distribution: Widespread across Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia; ubiquitous in Indian skies.
interesting_facts: Can soar effortlessly for hours using city thermal updrafts without flapping.
Known for lightning-fast aerial swoops to snatch food directly from human hands or plates.

description: A small woodland goshawk with pale blue-grey upperparts, fine rufous-brown barring on whitish underparts, and ruby-red eyes in adult males.
habitat: Open deciduous forest, groves, agricultural tree belts, plantations, and parks.
diet: Lizards, squirrels, mice, small passerine birds, and large insects.
distribution: Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: A swift ambush predator that hunts from a concealed leafy branch.
Historically prized in falconry across the Indian subcontinent for its agility and courage.

description: A medium cuckoo whose plumage closely mimics the Shikra hawk with barred underparts, yellow eye-rings, and grey upperparts.
habitat: Deciduous forests, river valleys, orchards, and heavily wooded gardens.
diet: Hairy caterpillars, beetles, bugs, and wild fruit.
distribution: Endemic to the Indian subcontinent.
interesting_facts: Colloquially known as the 'Brainfever bird' for its persistent, shrill three-note call that repeats day and night.
Its close mimicry of the predatory Shikra allows it to alarm and displace babbler hosts when laying eggs.

description: A tiny, uniformly greyish-brown swift with long swept-back crescent wings and a deeply forked slender tail.
habitat: Open lowlands, villages, and farmland with abundant palmyra or coconut palm trees.
diet: Tiny aerial flying insects caught continuously in high-speed flight.
distribution: Indian subcontinent, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia.
interesting_facts: Its entire lifecycle is tied to palm fronds; it glues its miniature nest to the underside of palm leaves using sticky saliva.
Its feet are so reduced it cannot perch on branches, only cling vertically to foliage.

description: A ghostly pale nocturnal raptor with a distinctive heart-shaped white facial disc, golden-buff and grey mottled back, and snowy underparts.
habitat: Agricultural barnyards, historic ruins, temple towers, and dry scrub country.
diet: Rats, mice, voles, shrews, and small birds.
distribution: Worldwide across all continents except Antarctica.
interesting_facts: Possesses asymmetric ear placement enabling pinpoint three-dimensional acoustic tracking in total darkness.
Feather fringes have microscopic velvety serrations that eliminate flight noise for silent hunting.

description: A small nocturnal owl with prominent feathered ear-tufts, finely vermiculated grey-brown bark-like plumage, and dark brown eyes.
habitat: Deciduous woodlands, groves, overgrown village orchards, and mature suburban gardens.
diet: Beetles, moths, grasshoppers, spiders, and occasionally small geckos.
distribution: Resident across India, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
interesting_facts: Emits a distinct single-note resonant frog-like hoot: 'what?' repeated at regular multi-second intervals.
Its plumage mimics tree bark so perfectly that it becomes nearly invisible when roosting against a trunk.
